text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on May 19 in history:
1536 - Anne Boleyn, the second of King Henry VIII's wives, was beheaded for adultery.
1643 - The Spanish were heavily defeated by the French under the Duke of Enghien at the battle of Rocroi. The Spanish infantry were destroyed, thus ending their supremacy.
1643 - The towns of Connecticut, Plymouth and New Haven formed a Confederation of the United Colonies of New England as protection in the wars with the Indians.
1795 - James Boswell, Scottish diarist and biographer and companion to Dr Samuel Johnson, died. His famous biography "Life of Johnson" was published in 1791.
1802 - In France, Napoleon created the Legion d'Honneur, an order of distinction for civil or military service.
1861 - Dame Nellie Melba, Australian operatic soprano, born as Helen Porter Mitchell. Her career took her to London's Covent Garden and New York's Metropolitan. She retired in 1926.

1890 - Ho Chi Minh, influential communist leader, born as Nguyen That Thanh. In Vietnam, he played a leading role in the struggle that ended with the French defeat in 1954. He became president of North Vietnam from 1954-69.
1898 - William Ewart Gladstone, British statesman and prime minister four times, died. An advocate of social and political reform, he tried without success to bring home rule to Ireland.
1900 - Tonga was annexed by Britain.
1906 - The Simplon Tunnel through the Alps between Italy and Switzerland was officially opened by the King of Italy and the president of the Swiss Republic.
1925 - Malcolm X, militant U.S. civil rights leader who advocated race pride and black nationalism, born as Malcolm Little.
1934 - In Bulgaria, an authoritarian regime was created after General Kimon Gheorgiev together with the nationalist organisation Zveno seized power in a coup.

1935 - T. E. (Thomas Edward) Lawrence, known as Lawrence of Arabia, died following a motorcycle accident six days previously. Famed for his military exploits during World War One which he wrote about in his "Seven Pillars of Wisdom".
1958 - Ronald Colman, English actor of stage and screen, died. Best known for his roles in "Random Harvest", "The Lost Horizon" and "A Double Life" for which he won an Oscar.
1974 - In France, Valery Giscard d'Estaing won the second round of presidential elections, defeating Francois Mitterrand.
1986 - South African forces raided what they claimed were ANC bases in Botswana, Zambia and Zimbabwe.
1992 - Two doctors who performed an autopsy on John F. Kennedy, confirmed that the president was killed by two bullets fired from above and behind.
1993 - U.S. government recognised the Angolan government after its democratic strides and urged UNITA to negotiate peace.
1994 - Malawi's aged, autocratic President Kamuzu Banda conceded victory to opposition leader Bakili Muluzi after more than 30 years of iron-fisted rule.

1994 - Jacqueline Kennedy Onassis, queen of a long-lost American Camelot and a world-wide symbol of jet-set glamour, died. In 1953, she married the future President John F. Kennedy and in 1968, five years after his assassination, she married shipping tycoon Aristotle Onassis.
